question: In ESOI, intents are meaningful containers of a set of specifications. For human understanding, they serve as a personal category of interest or relate to a tangible container such as an organization.
What is a specific phrase which distinguishes the topic of the intent from other intents?
What is this intent manifesting in present tense? e.g. "I am ..." or "The world is ..." Any subject and verb can be used.

A general category like "parenting" or "career." An intent is also not an organization itself, rather the container of specification that clarifies why the organization exists (as a solution and implementation within an intent). In this example, different versions of the same organization can be documented as separate alternative implementations.
A description of what motivated the intent. A challenge, difficulty, or description of how an ideal is not reached.

A decision, task, recommendation, or component, but all of these can *have* problems.
Ideals that oppose at least one aspect of the problem, Solutions that would solve at least one aspect of the problem
A definition of how one or more problems can be addressed to fulfill the intent.

What endusers of the relevant solution directly interact with. The solution provides an interface on top of the implementation. A structure solution defines how solution's will define interfaces.
A definition of the future state implied by the intent, in a particular dimension or aspect.
What's a combined noun with adjective that represents the ideal's direction of interest?
What does this ideal ask for?
Describe what it would be like to experience this ideal.

A practical metric or solution, or technology.
Problems the ideal opposes.

A practical way to measure the distance between the implementations of a solution and an ideal which the solution was defined to achieve. Alternative implementations are compared via metrics. Note: Metrics can also be solutions, as metrics themselves may be refined over time with alternative implementations (including dataset versions).
